query: What kidney care programs are available for a 65-year-old patient?

match_criteria.reason: opa_program_lookup uses Claude + Web Search, not vector retrieval

expert_answer: For a 65-year-old patient with kidney concerns, the Ontario Renal Network (now part of Ontario Health) provides comprehensive chronic kidney disease (CKD) management programs. The KidneyWise Clinical Toolkit supports primary care providers in identifying, detecting, and managing CKD patients. Referral to nephrology is recommended for: eGFR <30, rapid kidney function decline (eGFR <45 with >5 decline within 6 months), ACR >60, or 5-year Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE) ≥5%. Primary care providers can refer patients using the Outpatient Nephrology Referral Form. The Ontario Renal Network provides person-centered kidney care services throughout the kidney care continuum, including CKD management programs, dialysis services, and transplant coordination. Age 65+ is within standard eligibility for all kidney care programs. Cite: Ontario Health (Ontario Renal Network) https://www.ontariohealth.ca/clinical/renal.html and https://www.ontariorenalnetwork.ca

query: What cancer screening programs are recommended for an average-risk 50-year-old?
expected_answer_elements: Cite: Ontario Health Cancer Care Ontario
expert_answer: For an average-risk 50-year-old in Ontario, the following cancer screening programs are recommended: (1) Colorectal Cancer Screening: FIT (fecal immunochemical test) every 2 years for ages 50-74. The FIT replaced gFOBT as of December 2019. When colorectal cancer is caught early, 9 out of 10 people can be cured. (2) Breast Cancer Screening (for women): Mammography every 2 years through the Ontario Breast Screening Program (OBSP) for ages 50-74. No referral needed for average-risk women age 50-74. (3) Cervical Screening (for people with a cervix): Starting March 3, 2025, HPV testing replaced Pap tests as the primary cervical screening test. Screening begins at age 25 and continues every 5 years (previously every 3 years with Pap tests). All screening programs are OHIP-covered at no cost. Contact ColonCancerCheck, OBSP screening sites, or primary care providers for appointments. Cite: Ontario Health (Cancer Care Ontario) https://www.cancercareontario.ca

query: What cardiac rehab and diabetes education programs are available for a post-MI patient?
expected_answer_elements: Cite: Ontario Health cardiac and diabetes programs
expert_answer: Post-MI patients in Ontario have access to two key programs: (1) Cardiac Rehabilitation: Six-month programs requiring physician referral, providing comprehensive nurse case management, medical care, supervised exercise programming, dietary counselling, lifestyle education, and psychological services. Evidence shows cardiac rehab reduces total and cardiac mortality in patients with coronary artery disease. Standards are set by CorHealth Ontario (formerly Cardiac Care Network). Programs accept referrals for acute coronary syndrome (STEMI, Non-STEMI), PCI, CABG, and other cardiac events. (2) Diabetes Education Programs: Available to adults 18+ diagnosed with diabetes or at high risk. Programs are open to public with primary care provider referral or self-referral if no primary care provider. Services include individual and group counselling by Diabetes Nurse Educators and Registered Dietitians, with life plans to minimize symptoms and prevent complications. Both programs are OHIP-covered at no cost. Coordination between programs occurs through multidisciplinary teams. Cite: Ontario Health cardiac care https://www.ontariohealth.ca/clinical/cardiac-stroke-vascular.html and Ontario Diabetes Education Programs https://www.ontario.ca/page/diabetes-education-program

query: What mental health programs are available for adults with depression?
expected_answer_elements: Cite: Ontario Health mental health programs
expert_answer: Adults with depression in Ontario can access free, publicly-funded cognitive-behavioural therapy through the Ontario Structured Psychotherapy Program (OSP). The program is OHIP-covered for adults 18+ and treats depression, low mood, generalized anxiety, social anxiety, panic attacks, health anxiety, obsessive-compulsive concerns, post-traumatic stress, and specific fears. Services include: (1) Self-led resources guided by coach/therapist: BounceBack (phone-based with workbooks and bi-weekly coaching), Clinician-Assisted Bibliotherapy (phone-based with CBT self-help guide and weekly 30-minute sessions), and Internet-based CBT (online modules guided by therapist). (2) Individual or group cognitive-behavioural therapy (in-person or virtual sessions). Most people begin with self-led resources; the care team monitors closely and can transition clients to individual/group therapy if needed. Registration: Primary care provider referral or self-referral available. Contact local OSP programs through Ontario Health regions. Interpretive services available in many languages. Cite: Ontario Health OSP Program https://www.ontariohealth.ca/clinical/mental-health-addictions/structured-psychotherapy.html

query: What stroke prevention and rehabilitation programs exist in Ontario?
expert_answer: Ontario has a comprehensive Ontario Stroke System organized into 11 regional stroke systems providing prevention, acute care, and rehabilitation services. The system is led by CorHealth Ontario (formerly Ontario Stroke Network merged with Cardiac Care Network in 2016-2017). Each region has designated Regional Stroke Centres and District Stroke Centres providing tertiary and organized stroke care based on evidence-based standards. Services include: (1) Primary Prevention: Risk factor management and education through primary care and specialized clinics. (2) Acute Stroke Care: Regional stroke centers with 24/7 access to stroke teams, thrombolysis, and interventional procedures. (3) Stroke Rehabilitation: Community Stroke Rehabilitation Programs providing recovery support, home environment adaptation, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, and connection to other services. Programs are designed to help patients through recovery and reduce residual disability. Access: Through hospital emergency departments for acute care, and through healthcare provider referrals or Ontario Health atHome for rehabilitation services. All services are OHIP-covered. Cite: Ontario Health cardiac, stroke and vascular care https://www.ontariohealth.ca/clinical/cardiac-stroke-vascular.html
